description: I'm Srishti, building Earth Listens for The Earth Information Jukebox: an instrument that turns decades of NASA Earth data into music, so anyone can hear climate change and blind or low-vision learners can explore data without charts. Our first scene (NASA GISS temperature) already works. Looking for: a sound designer or musician, someone with Earth-science or satellite-data experience (sea ice, vegetation), and an accessibility tester. All skill levels welcome!
summary: Earth Listens turns NASA Earth data into sound so people can hear climate change instead of only reading about it. Visitors choose a scene, scrub through time, and listen to decades of real observations as music: calm when conditions are near the historical baseline, tense when they are extreme. The Arctic scene plays NSIDC September sea ice extent from 1979 to 2026 against a data-driven polar visual with a ghost outline of the 1979 extent. The temperature scene plays NASA GISS global temperature anomalies from 1880 to 2025 beside a stripe for every year. "Earth song of your life" plays the record from any birth year to today and lets users save it as an audio file. It addresses The Earth Information Jukebox challenge and opens climate data to blind and low-vision users, with full keyboard control, screen-reader announcements, and no sound until the user presses play. Every value comes from official NASA or NSIDC records, and the sound mapping is documented and tested.
details:
What it does: Earth Listens is a static web instrument. Pick a scene, drag through time or press play, and hear each year's real value as music. Pitch follows the value, distance from a historical baseline adds tension, year-to-year change adds rhythm, and variability adds texture. Moment buttons jump to the record low or warmest year, compare mode plays two periods in the left and right ear, and "Earth song of your life" plays from a birth year to the latest year and can be saved.

Data: NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 global temperature anomaly (1880-2025) and the NSIDC Sea Ice Index v4 September Northern Hemisphere extent (1979-2026). Values are used unaltered; sources, access dates, and the 2025 change in NSIDC's upstream input product are documented in the app and README.

Accessibility: fully keyboard operable, labelled controls, live-region announcements, reduced-motion support, and no audio before a user gesture. We have not yet tested with blind or low-vision users and say so in the README.

Tools: TypeScript, Vite, Tone.js (Web Audio), Vitest, ESLint, GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages.

Limits: we did not include a vegetation scene because the needed data required authorization and processing we could not verify in time. Audio download was verified only in Chromium.

AI use: we used AI coding agents (GitHub Copilot) to write much of the code, tests, and documentation. Our team chose the concept, sourced and checked the data, specified the sound design, and reviewed and tested the result by ear and by keyboard. Code, documentation text, and the generated audio are acknowledged as AI-assisted in the README, docs/AI_USE.md, and the app.
